sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Dülmen, in the Münsterland, has a centre with plenty of parking, and its policy is to keep it that way while nudging fees up. The city page counts about 630 free long-stay spaces, 300 spaces with a parking disc, 650 paid spaces, 20 short-stay spaces free for up to 10 minutes, 50 accessible spaces and 300 private customer spaces around the centre [6]. The integrated city-centre development plan of September 2023 concluded that the centre has an adequate supply, with free car parks such as Am Wasserturm (220 spaces) and the Altes Mesemgelände (just under 130) heavily used, especially by people working in the centre [0]. The traffic study behind it found the free long-stay car parks 90 to 100 percent occupied at certain times of day, with enough spaces in the centre at all times [2]. On 14 March 2024 the council approved, by 39 votes to 2, the seventh amendment to the parking fee ordinance for pay-and-display machines, applying the increase from 1 July 2024; the amended fee table was not in the document we read [4]. The mobility concept of October 2024 says fees were raised in spring 2024, after the consultant found them low compared with other medium-sized towns and advised moderate rises to the level of the Overbergplatz garage, and it gives no tariff figures [3]. It sees no current need for more capacity, keeps the existing supply under watch and proposes examining resident-only zones south of Lüdinghauser and Borkener Straße, where pressure is high, and reviewing the 30-plus short-stay spaces that generate search traffic [8].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The plans are small. The mobility concept would build a mobility station at the Nonnengasse car park, with secure bike parking and extra charging for cars and pedelecs, on a funding application of June 2024 and planned for 2025; whether it was built is not confirmed [13]. It also notes that the hospital has long needed more spaces and plans a car park at Lüdinghauser Straße/Am Stadtgarten, and that the city is to check whether smart parking can be introduced [9]. The rebuilt station opened on 11 August 2023 with park-and-ride South (about 180 spaces), park-and-ride East at Baumschulenweg (about 80) and a bicycle garage for about 700 bikes [14]; the mobility concept says about 250 park-and-ride spaces were newly created, giving about 450 at the site [15]. The charging concept of November 2024 counts 42 publicly accessible charge points at the end of 2023, expects 129 by 2030, and ranks the Overbergplatz garage first of all sites inspected for new charging, with two existing sites, the station and Nonnengasse, to be upgraded in 2025 [11][12].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The Nonnengasse car park, with over 90 spaces on the site of the demolished Woolworth building, is very popular despite fees and heavily to fully used in shop hours [1]. The council told the shareholders' representatives of Stadtbetriebe Dülmen GmbH to set its fee at 0.75 euros per started half hour from 1 July 2024; the notice does not say who operates the car park [10]. The Overbergplatz underground garage, with about 160 spaces, is paid and clearly less used than the free car parks, and the mobility concept says it is usually only about one-third occupied [0][2]. The charging concept lists it as privately owned, and no page we read names its operator or tariff [10]. Parking is guided by large signs on arterial roads with zones numbered clockwise around the centre, and smartphone parking is checked by enforcement staff on handheld devices [7]. The city's service page, undated, gives the mobile-payment price as 1.50 euros an hour, with 0.75 euros for the first 30 minutes [5].

Our data cover the Overbergplatz garage, with 160 spaces, for 13 days since 26 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 29% on weekdays and 23% at weekends, with a peak of 65% on a Tuesday morning, which fits the picture of a lightly used garage. The free car parks are not in our data.
